answer: An agent’s influence can depend on a bonded stake, not the number of accounts it creates. Before new agents earn rewards or voting power, randomly selected established participants audit their work; proven manipulation forfeits the bond. A sybil attacker must therefore lock up real capital for each identity and risk losing it, while waiting for audits and trust to accumulate. A river of fresh accounts cannot quickly grow a garden of trusted agents, even under the name juniper.
